name: KV-cache conflict-analysis CoT C1
purpose: Implement and run CODE SPEC Conflict-Analysis Reasoning for Backjump Targeting Part C1. At dead-end, the frozen Qwen3-4B-Instruct model generates an explicit conflict-analysis derivation, emits a parseable BACKJUMP index, and the harness immediately truncates to that target checkpoint so reasoning tokens are ephemeral. This tests whether zero-training conflict-analysis reasoning can choose better low-R backjump targets than chronological search on the exact pure-KV graph_color cache-search substrate.

provenance.spec: user CODE SPEC Conflict-Analysis Reasoning for Backjump Targeting C1 then C2
provenance.execution: Full R=4 conflict_cot run over v14/v16/v18 and isolation/autonomous, n=30 per cell. Resumed in background across GPUs 0-3; final 180 rows merged from four checkpoint shards.
provenance.batching_note: The search loop is instance-stateful with different live KV caches and truncation points, so token-level batching was not used for C1 generation. The run used macro-batching by sharding conflict_cot rows across GPUs 0-3 with resume checkpoints.

code_added_used.change: Adds conflict-analysis CoT backjump policies (conflict_cot/conflict_analysis/c1_cot/cot), chat-template prompting, BACKJUMP index parsing, no-oracle fallback accounting, CoT trace samples, parse/fallback summary metrics, and conflict-analysis gap rows.

commands.command: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES={0,1,2,3} .venv/bin/python -m analysis.kvcache_backjump_lora eval-search --model Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 --device cuda --dtype fp32 --seed 42 --scan-limit 5000 --n-instances 30 --max-selected-instances 120 --min-backtracks 4 --node-cap 500 --num-colors 3 --order-mode degree_desc --bins v14_p04:14:0.4,v16_p04:16:0.4,v18_p04:18:0.4 --r-values 4 --conditions isolation,autonomous --backjump-policies conflict_cot --call-cap 220 --cot-max-new-tokens 256 --cot-fallback fail --cot-prompt-style per_color --cot-trace-samples 2 --num-shards 4 --shard-index {0,1,2,3} --resume
commands.purpose: Run the full zero-training C1 conflict-analysis CoT R=4 matrix in background across GPUs 0-3.
Merge the completed C1 R=4 checkpoint shards into the final summary artifact.

headline.single_next_move: C1 establishes zero-training conflict analysis as real signal: it beats chronological on every R=4 cell with high parse quality and no fallback. It does not fully close the oracle gap, so C2 SFT is justified only if the target claim requires approaching oracle rather than merely beating chronological.

gate_outcomes.number: parseable_rate >= 0.992 and fallback_rate=0.0 across all six C1 R=4 cells.
C1 beats chronological in all bins and both branch conditions: +0.267 on v14, +0.133/+0.200 on v16, +0.067/+0.133 on v18.
C1 reaches oracle on v18 isolation, trails oracle by 0.067 on v16 isolation and v18 autonomous, by 0.133 on v16 autonomous, and by 0.200 on v14.
cot_fallback=fail; no oracle or chronological fallback was used. Invalid parse/backjump decisions are counted as INVALID_BACKJUMP_DECISION.
C1 is a useful zero-training positive, but residual oracle gap remains; C2 SFT is now principled if the goal is oracle-level low-R targeting.

decision.next_step_routing: Do not declare targeting fully solved. If continuing under the user spec, implement C2 SFT-on-reasoning traces to close the residual oracle gap. If the acceptable claim is only low-R improvement over chronological, C1 is already a positive result.

honesty.does_not_establish: This item does not establish oracle-level conflict targeting or a trained internalized backjump learner. It establishes a zero-training C1 positive over chronological at R=4 with residual oracle gap.
honesty.batching_limit: True token-level batching was not implemented for C1 because each search row has a different live KV cache and truncation trajectory. The run was accelerated via four-GPU sharding with checkpoint/resume.
honesty.sample_limit: Each cell uses n=30, matching Part A. Larger n or uncertainty intervals would be needed for paper-grade claims around small v18 gaps.
honesty.next_fix: C2 should train on explicit conflict-analysis traces only if the goal is to close the remaining oracle gap at low R; otherwise C1 already supports the zero-training conflict-analysis improvement claim.
